chunks: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Maktab narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Warraq narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Aban ibn Mahran narrated to us, he said: Abdullah ibn Abi Sa'id al-Warraq narrated to us, he said: Fudayl ibn Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, he said: Yunus ibn Abi Ya'qub al-Abdi narrated to us, from his father, from Qanbar, the servant of Ali (peace be upon him), who said:

I entered with Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) to Uthman ibn Affan, and he desired seclusion, so Ali (peace be upon him) signaled to me to step aside, so I stepped aside not far away. Then Uthman began to reproach Ali (peace be upon him) while Ali was lowering his head. Then Uthman turned to him and said: 'What is it with you that you do not speak?' He said: 'If I am to speak, I will not say except that which you dislike, and you will not have from me except what you like.'

key_terms.مُطْرَقٌ: lowering his head (in humility or contemplation)

ai.seo_question: What was Ali's response to Uthman's reproach regarding his silence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, this narration captures the nuanced political tension between Imam Ali and Caliph Uthman, where Ali’s strategic silence served as a diplomatic tool to preserve harmony while withholding his full counsel. The phrase highlights the Shia scholarly understanding of *hikmah* (wisdom) in governance, illustrating how Ali balanced truthfulness with social cohesion during the early Caliphate.
